trick: Learn the superlatives, because that is what gets asked. Largest Jupiter, hottest Venus, smallest and nearest to the Sun Mercury, red Mars, ringed Saturn, tilted on its side Uranus. And the Sun is a star, which quietly answers a surprising number of questions.

data.prompt: True or false? Mark each statement about the solar system and space.

items.statement: Venus is the hottest planet in the solar system.
items.why: Its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat, so it is hotter than Mercury even though Mercury is nearer the Sun.

items.statement: Pluto is counted as the ninth planet of the solar system.
items.why: It was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006, so the solar system has eight planets.

items.statement: Neil Armstrong was the first human being to walk on the Moon.
items.why: He stepped onto the surface on 20 July 1969 during the Apollo 11 mission.

items.statement: Chandrayaan and Mangalyaan are missions of ISRO.
items.why: Chandrayaan went to the Moon and Mangalyaan to Mars, making India the first country to reach Mars orbit on its first attempt.

items.statement: A light year measures time, not distance.
items.why: Despite the name it measures distance: how far light travels in one year, about 9.46 million million kilometres.

trick: Instrument questions answer themselves if you read the name. A barometer measures baros, weight or pressure; a thermometer measures therme, heat; a seismograph writes down seismos, an earthquake. The Greek root is the answer.
